title: Side Effects of Psychotherapy: Survey on the Frequency and Nature of Negative Effects in Outpatient Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Children and Adolescents
summary:
Numerous studies have shown that psychotherapy is effective for children and adolescents, as it helps most children and adolescents feel better and reduce their symptoms. However, negative effects can also occur in psychotherapy in rare cases. To date, there has been little research into how often and to what extent negative effects occur in psychotherapy for children and adolescents. Negative effects can be divided into four categories: 
- Side effects: The therapy is carried out correctly, but negative effects still occur.
- Malpractice: The therapy is not carried out in accordance with guidelines, resulting in negative effects.
- Lack of patient-therapist fit: No trusting relationship develops between the child/adolescent and the therapist does not develop, resulting in negative effects.
- Therapeutic misconduct: The therapist behaves unethically, resulting in negative effects.
The first category (side effects) in particular has been very little researched in children and adolescents to date. The aim of this study is to investigate negative effects associated with psychotherapy in children and adolescents for the first time in Germany. The following questions will be answered:
1) How often do children and adolescents experience negative effects in psychotherapy? In what catergory do these negative effects occur? 
2) What side effects of psychotherapy do children, adolescents, and their primary caregivers report?
3) Do children and adolescents perceive the same negative effects as their caregivers?

interventions.name: After every 10th therapy session, participants (children/adolescents and their primary caregivers) fill out an adapted version of the Inventory for Assessing Negative Effects of Psychotherapy for Children and Parents (Kinder-INEP; Bieda et al., 2018) anonymously at home. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- All children and adolescents who are currently receiving outpatient cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) at the Outpatient Psychotherapy Clinic for Children and Adolescents at the University of Trier are eligible to participate (currently ongoing psychotherapy).
- By the time of the first measurement, at least 10 appointments had taken place at the Outpatient Psychotherapy Clinic for Children and Adolescents at the University of Trier.
Exclusion criteria:
None.
